newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada 1997 housing starts better than forecast.
newsitem.headline: Canada 1997 housing starts better than forecast.

text.p: Housing starts in major Canadian urban centers should increase by 15 percent in 1997, better than the 7.2 percent forecast at the end of 1996, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Thursday.

The semi-annual report for Canadian cities said starts would rise in 19 of 27 major centers. The outlook for custom-built homes for repeat buyers was even better, to climb 17 percent and to be up in 22 of the 27 major centers.
Housing starts rose by 14 percent in the cities in 1996, CMHC said.
Resales should also rise, by a forecast 4.5 percent, this year after a 24 percent jump in 1996.
"Enthusiastic repeat buyers have now given strength to the new single market," said CMHC Market Analyst Bruno Duhamel.

"Consumer confidence will continue to strengthen in most centers as interest rates stay relatively low, house prices remain affordable and employment continues to improve, particularly for younger workers."
